title: Italy's AI and physical AI companies

lede.t: A census of 74 AI and physical AI companies headquartered in Italy that have closed at least a seed round. Each profile records what the company sells and to whom, whose models it runs on, its funding, scale, its base in Italy and one main use case with impact indicators. A companion to the I³/NYC census of New York City.

sub.t: Eight findings computed from the profiles below. The census is a curated sample of Italy's funded AI companies, not a complete register; see the method notes for what is missing.

findings.title: Milan is the hub, Turin the second pole

body.t: companies are based in Milan, with €654M raised. Turin has 8, most of them out of the Politecnico's I3P incubator. Rome's €432M is almost all Exein.

findings.title: Italian companies build their own models

body.t: Of the 42 companies that disclose a model strategy,
train in-house, often vision, forecasting or robotics models rather than LLMs. Only 7 build mainly on external models. Domyn and Expert.ai develop their own language technology.

body.t: , TeamSystem bought Normo.ai, Stirling Square bought iConsulting for over €200M. Italy's largest listing of the period, Bending Spoons, went to Nasdaq.

caveats.t: Companies whose product is AI or depends on it, with headquarters in Italy, and at least one disclosed seed or later round (about €500K or more) or €2M or more raised in total. Older platforms that added AI are included and labelled AI-enabled.
A company counts when its legal and operating headquarters are in Italy. Italian-founded companies headquartered in London, the US, Switzerland or the Netherlands are listed separately, not counted.

Italy counts nearly 15,000 AI-focused firms. This census profiles 74 of the funded ones that could be verified within a fixed research budget. Names that were reviewed and left out are listed below with the reason.
Amounts are in euros. Rounds announced in dollars are converted at about $1 = €0.86, so figures can differ slightly from press headlines.

Company announcements, CDP Venture Capital, Growth Capital and Italian Tech Alliance, Dealroom, tech.eu, EU-Startups, StartupItalia, Startupbusiness, Milano Finanza, Teleborsa and trade press. Each profile links its sources.
18 profiles are rated high and 17 low. Low means the location, the founding year or the funding rests on a single aggregator. Low-confidence rows carry a label.

10 companies have no total-raised figure, so sums understate. Domyn's total is equity only; its reported 2026 package is mostly debt. Valuations are rarely disclosed in Italy: only Exein and Domyn have a reported one.
Only 5 companies publish a revenue figure and 16 a headcount; these are mostly company statements or LinkedIn counts.
Coded from what companies and press say. 32 companies disclose nothing usable and are left as undisclosed.
Company site links are shown only where the domain was confirmed; others are left out rather than guessed.
Research closed October 16, 2026. Founding year is missing for 22 companies.
